text:
aj: Heads-up — staging started hitting OOMs on long-chat loadtest around 06:10. Memory climbs steadily across requests even after KV cache evictions. Not sure if it's fragmentation or a real leak.

sam: ugh. which build? any kernel-picker changes recently?

aj: rolling canary from yesterday (opt-kernels v2). Also bumped workspace from 512MB -> 768MB for safety.

maria: I saw a similar trend last week when we added the continuous-batching tweak. Allocator histograms looked weird. Could be small-slab retention.

kai: paste of recent nsys summary I grabbed:
```
Time(%)  Calls     Avg       Min       Max     Name
12.3     alloc     1.2MB     128B      2MB     cudamalloc
8.9      free      0.8MB     64B       1.5MB   cudafree
45.6     kernel    0.5ms     0.1ms     10ms    matmul

Resident GPU memory: 14.2GB -> 16.1GB over 1k requests
Active allocations (sample): 42k -> 57k small buffers (<4KB)
```
kai: that spike in small buffers seems suspicious — kv cache eviction should release large tensors but small temporary buffers might be leaked by workspace reuse logic.

diego: Could be our reuse pool not returning buffers to the global allocator when kernel path switches (kernel selector path A vs B). We added path-local pools for perf.

sam: Good call. If pool keeps growing but doesn't coalesce, fragmentation looks like leak. We need a repro script to stress small alloc/free churn and toggling kernel-selector.

aj: I put together a tiny repro harness (runs on single GPU):
```bash
# stress-repro.sh
for i in {1..2000}; do
  python -c '\"from runtime import serve; serve.request(seq_len=1024, kernel_policy=\'auto\')\"'
  if (( i % 200 == 0 )); then
    python -c 'from runtime import kv; kv.evict_all()'
  fi
 done
```
aj: When I run that, resident mem climbs ~1.8GB over the loop and doesn't drop after evictions. nvprof snapshot shows rising #allocs of <4KB buffers.

maria: Can you run with ENV VERBOSE_ALLOC=1 and dump allocator stats every 100 iters? We have code to print slab buckets and free list lengths.

aj: Ran that. Key excerpt: 
```
[alloc-stats] slab_4k: used=7200 free=30 high_water=9000
[alloc-stats] slab_8k: used=1200 free=5 high_water=1300
[pool] path_A: pooled=8200 path_B: pooled=2400
```
aj: free counts tiny, high_water growing.

kai: That looks like pool growth. Two hypotheses: (1) path-local pools leak because we never drain them on policy switch; (2) allocator coalescing disabled when using per-path pools -> fragmentation.

diego: I can instrument pool drain on policy switch and run quick compare. Also try forcing global pooling only (env POOL_MODE=global) to see if growth stops.

sam: Also test with workspace cap smaller (workspace_max=256MB) to force buffers to be returned earlier. If growth slows, muckiness in workspace sizing.

aj: Quick test results: POOL_MODE=global -> growth stabilizes (resident stays ~14.4GB). workspace_max=256MB -> still growth but slower.

maria: so global pooling helps. That implies path-local pools were hoarding buffers. Not necessarily a leak, more mis-accounted retention. But we still saw small free counts — fragmentation risk remains.

kai: One more profiler trace: when kernel selector flips to path_B, we see many tiny allocations without frees inside a single request. Looks like path_B uses a helper that requests ephemeral buffers and caches them in the pool but never releases on request end.

diego: I pushed a candidate patch that calls pool->return_all() at the end of request processing for path_B. Can someone run the loadtest with opt-kernels v2 + patch?

aj: Running now on staging canary-2. Patch applied. Early numbers: after 1k iters, resident stable, alloc histogram flat. Need a longer run but promising.

sam: Nice. If that fixes it, we should add unit test to simulate many path switches and assert pool sizes bounded. Also add a periodic pool-scrubber in runtime to reclaim rarely-used slabs.

maria: Agreed. Also we should add a dedicated perf regression alert for small-buffer count growth (threshold e.g., >10k persistent small allocations or 5% increase over baseline).

kai: For root-cause doc, capture: kernel-selector change introduced path-local pooling optim for hot path, but path_B didn't return buffers on request teardown -> hoarding -> apparent leak. Evidence: allocator stats + nsys samples + POOL_MODE=global experiment.

aj: I'll open PR with repro harness, test, and the patch. PR will include: how to run stress script, env flags we used, nvprof/NSYS samples, and the allocator trace excerpts.

diego: I'll follow up with a stress job overnight (10k iters) and add a scrubber as fallback.

infra-bot: deploy canary-2 -> staging (sha: a1b2c3d) at 07:14 UTC :white_check_mark:

sam: Thanks all. Follow-up items: PR + tests (aj), overnight stress (diego), perf alert (maria), design doc for pool semantics (kai).

aj: Thanks — will keep thread updated with PR link and full nvprof captures. :thumbsup:
